policy_title: Increase DEFRA budget and fund nature-based solutions
stated: Increase DEFRA’s budget by £1.5bn to fund the Environment Agency and Natural England. Restore rivers, take a nature-based approach to flood prevention and storm overflows, and develop a soil health monitoring programme for England.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push to restore rivers and take a nature-based solutions approach to the prevention of flooding and storm overflows. We would increase DEFRA’s budget by £1.5bn, allowing an increase in funding for the Environment Agency and Natural England, to support the vital work they do to protect our environment. This would include developing a soil health monitoring programme for England, to match those in Scotland and Wales, to assess and understand changes in the health of soil over time.

bearing_set.reason: Directly funds river restoration, flood prevention via nature-based solutions, storm overflow management, and soil health monitoring — all core clean environment indicators (water quality, emissions/land carbon, nature).
A £1.5bn increase to DEFRA's budget is a material spending commitment; without a specified funding source it plausibly widens the funded/borrowed gap, moving the debt-path indicator.

Nature-based flood prevention protects property, infrastructure and farmland from flood damage (a concrete economic mechanism); soil health monitoring supports agricultural productivity — both move O13's living-standards and productivity indicators non-negligibly.

membership_note: Primary bearing is O6 (the explicit environmental target); O12 captures the fiscal cost of the spending commitment; O13 reflects the economic protection and productivity gains from flood resilience and soil health. No other fundamental clears the non-negligible threshold.
